source.text: Preoperative meds plus Vicodin for pain.
Routine postoperative instructions given and said follow up will be in four weeks in the office.

diagnosis_explanation: Your period bleeding was heavier than normal. This is called menorrhagia. You also had painful periods. This is called dysmenorrhea. You have small fibroids in your uterus. Fibroids are small lumps of muscle in the uterus. They are usually not cancer.
medication_rationale:
Vicodin:
This medicine is given to help with pain.
It is a pain reliever.
You may feel sleepy or dizzy.
Your mouth may feel dry.
Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.
Also call if you feel very confused.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will feel tired and sore after surgery.
- Rest often is important for healing.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 10 pounds.
- Avoid strenuous activity. This includes heavy housework.
- Walking around your home is encouraged.
- You may have light vaginal bleeding or spotting.
- Call your doctor if bleeding soaks a pad in one hour.
- Your goal is to walk a little more each day.

**Week 2:**
- You may start to feel a bit more energy.
- Pain should slowly get better each day.
- Continue to avoid heavy lifting and strenuous activity.
- Light walking is still good for you.
- You can return to light household tasks.
- Call your doctor for heavy bleeding or fever over 100.4 F.
- Your goal is to walk for 5 to 10 minutes twice a day.

**Week 3:**
- Most discomfort should be manageable now.
- You can likely do more around the house.
- Continue to avoid lifting more than 10 pounds.
- Avoid any activities that strain your belly.
- Keep up with your walking routine.
- Call your doctor if you have worsening pain or new swelling.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel a good improvement in energy.
- Most surgical pain should be gone.
- You can return to most normal activities.
- Check with your doctor before resuming sexual activity.
- Continue to avoid very heavy lifting for now.
- Your goal is to walk for 20 to 30 minutes daily.
- Call your doctor with any concerns about vaginal discharge.

**When to expect improvement:**
- You will feel better each week.
- Healing continues for several weeks.
- Most people return to normal life within 6 weeks.
- Keep following any instructions from your doctor.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Uncontrolled bleeding that will not stop: This needs urgent care now.
- Severe pain that will not stop: This needs urgent care now.
- Signs of stroke: face drooping, arm weakness, trouble speaking. Minutes matter.
- Loss of consciousness or fainting: Get help right away.
- Fast heart rate with dizziness: Call 911 right now.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Bleeding that is heavy and soaking pads: Change pads every hour.
- Passing blood clots larger than a golf ball: This needs review today.
- Severe cramping that is not helped by medicine: This needs review today.
- Feeling dizzy or lightheaded often: You may be losing too much blood.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild bleeding that is less than a heavy period: Manage at home.
- Questions about your pain medicine: Your nurse can help you plan.
- Cramping that is mild and slowly getting better: This is expected.
- Mild fatigue or feeling tired: This will improve with rest.
